Causes the target being hit to take extra DMG, which is not considered an attack.

Additional DMG
 is a type of 
damage
 dealt through certain abilities. Additional DMG is 
not
 considered an attack. In combat, Additional DMG is displayed as individual damage numbers separated from other damage sources.

There are two main sources of Additional DMG: Character's abilities, in which case it's calculated 
similarly to regular damage
, and Weakness Break, in which case it's calculated 
similarly to Break DMG
.

Character Additional DMG can score CRIT hits and is affected by 
Element
/All-type 
DMG Boost
. However, it is 
not
 affected by DMG Boost that is limited to certain DMG tags (e.g. 
Basic Attack
, 
Skill
, 
Ultimate
, 
Follow-Up Attack
, 
DoT
, etc.) unless specified.

's 

 
Frozen
 and 
Quantum

Entanglement

Weakness Break
 Additional DMG at the start of the target's turn. Additional DMG of Frozen and Entanglement triggered by Weakness Break cannot score CRIT hits and is 
not
 affected by DMG Boost.

 to each use their Elation Skill 1 time. If there are no units capable of using Elation Skills when Aha takes action, Aha will use "Let There Be Laughter."

Elation Skills
 in a fixed order based on their "Participant ID", from lowest to highest. Other effects that can trigger Elation Skills are also triggered in sequence during this time. After all Elation Skills are used or the battle is cleared, a card is displayed showing the total damage dealt by the Aha Instant, and the team's Punchline total is cleared with all Elation characters gaining a corresponding amount of 
Certified Banger

. When allies are hit, they regenerate a minor amount of Energy each hit.

Auto-Battle.text:
Auto-Battle

	

		

		
	

	

	
		
Type

	
	

Combat

Auto-Battle
 is a feature in 

Honkai: Star Rail

 that automatically controls the player's team during combat.

While Auto-Battle is active, usage and targeting of abilities are determined by a variety of factors, including Skill Points, enemy 
weaknesses
, enemy 
HP
, team HP, 
Status Effects
, etc.

Auto-Battle is unlocked during 
Simulated Universe: First Closed Beta
, but may become unavailable during certain story battles. It is also unavailable during battles in 
Aptitude Showcases
.

AI Logic

[

Common Logic

[

]

Skills
 are more likely to be used the more Skill Points the team has (except healing skills).

Healing skills favor characters with lower current HP percentage, and avoid characters with more than 80% current HP.

Damaging abilities favor enemies with matching weakness or are weakness broken.

This usually influences Single Target abilities to a greater extent than Blast abilities.

Single Target and Bounce 
Basic ATKs
 and Skills favor enemies with lower current HP percentage.

This usually influences Basic ATKs to a greater extent than Skills.

Blast abilities favor enemies with adjacent targets on both sides.

Ultimates
 are used immediately when available (except healing Ultimates).

Auto-Battle will not use Ultimates at 0 AV even if available, instead waiting for an ally or enemy to start their turn.

Single Target Ultimates favor enemies whose current HP percentage is between 20% and 80%.

Healing Ultimates are not used until an ally reaches 50% current HP.

Ultimate Priority

[

]

When multiple Ultimates are ready to be used at the same time, higher priority Ultimates are used first. If there are multiple Ultimates with the same priority level, they will be used from left to right based on team slot.

Certified Banger
 is a character-only 
buff
 and stat in 

Honkai: Star Rail

, exclusive to characters following the 
Path
 of 
Elation
. It allows them to deal additional instances of 
Elation DMG
 outside 
Aha Instants
 and is used to calculate the damage dealt for those instances.

Description

[

]

Characters participating in the 
Aha Instant
 gain the "Certified Banger" state. And the 
Punchline
 points from the current Aha Instant are taken into account for this state, lasting for 2 turns. Ability effects and 
Elation DMG
 produced by the "Certified Banger" state are calculated based on the Punchline points taken into account.
Punchline points taken into account for multiple "Certified Banger" states are combined for the calculation.
The duration of each "Certified Banger" state is tracked independently.

Certified Banger points typically last for 2 turns, tracked separately. It's possible to view when all of a character's current points are set to expire through their status effect list, and a total is displayed as a special graphic where 
Talent
 information typically is.

The primary method of obtaining Certified Banger is through Aha Instants. Following the use of all 
Elation Skills
, the team's Punchline tally is cleared, and all Elation characters in the team gain the corresponding amount of Certified Banger. Additionally, all Elation characters gain 20 Certified Banger points when entering battle, and certain characters can directly grant themselves or others Certified Banger points using their abilities.

If an Elation Character's Certified Banger points are above 0, certain abilities are activated which typically deal additional instances of Elation DMG based on their Certified Banger points.

The Punchline multiplier for Elation DMG is as follows:

CRIT Rate

Honkai: Star Rail

DoT
 and

-related DMG cannot CRIT.

5%
.

]

Other types of damage with their own damage formulas are:

Break DMG, Break DoT, and Break Additional DMG
 - Damage dealt by breaking an enemy's Toughness is calculated differently from normal DMG, scaling with the attacker's level and 
Break Effect
, and the enemy's max 
Toughness
.

Elation DMG
 - Elation DMG scales with the attacker's level like Break DMG. Additionally, instead of taking 
DMG Boost
 into account, it incorporates 
Elation
, 
Punchline
/
Certified Banger
, and 
Merrymake
.

True DMG
 - True DMG directly deals damage (based on another factor such as tallied DMG or Max HP) without being modified by any damage calculation multipliers.

tables.Description: When using the Ultimate, for every enemy on the field, additionally increases the Hits Per Action for the current Ultimate by 1 hit(s), up to a maximum increase of 5 hit(s).

This effect is triggered automatically when requirements are met. by 5. Upon its use, the DMG taken by all enemy targets increases by 12%, lasting for 2 turn(s).

tables.Name: Unexpected Hanging Paradox Unexpected Hanging Paradox
tables.Description: When triggering his Talent's Follow-up ATKFollow-Up ATKUnleashes an extra attack on the target. This effect is triggered automatically when requirements are met., first increases Aventurine's DEF by 40% for 2 turn(s), and additionally increases the Hits Per Action for his talent's Follow-up ATKFollow-Up ATKUnleashes an extra attack on the target. This effect is triggered automatically when requirements are met. by 3.

tables.Name: Arcadia Under Deep Seclusion Arcadia Under Deep Seclusion
tables.Description: While "Fuyuan" is on the field, reduces all enemies' All-Type RES by 20%. When "Fuyuan" attacks, additionally deals 4 instance(s) of DMG, with each instance dealing Fire DMG equal to 50% of Lingsha's ATK and 5 Toughness Reduction to one random enemy. This prioritizes targets with both Toughness greater than 0 and Fire Weakness.

tables.Name: Await for Years to Loom Await for Years to Loom
tables.Description: When Castorice or Netherwing deals DMG, increases Quantum RES PENRES PENWhen dealing DMG, ignore a part of the enemy target's resistance to the corresponding damage type. by 20%. During Netherwing's attacks, can reduce enemy Toughness regardless of Weakness Types. When breaking Weaknesses, triggers the Quantum Weakness Break effect. And the number of Bounces for Netherwing's Talent "Wings Sweep the Ruins" additionally increases by 3.

For every 1 PunchlinePunchlinePunchline is shared by the whole team. Damage RES

{\displaystyle \text{RES Multiplier} = 1 - (\text{RES}_\text{Target} - \text{RES PEN}_\text{Attacker})}

  

Typically, enemies will have 0% RES against types they are 
weak
 to and 20% RES against other types. There are a few exceptions to this rule, with these higher RES values usually being given to bosses and themed enemies. 
Apocalyptic Shadow
 enemies have a minimum of 40% Damage RES to types they are not weak to.

Since 
Version 4.0
, the maximum base Damage RES possessed by an enemy is 80%.

Damage RES ranges between -100% and 90%. Therefore, RES Multiplier ranges between 10% and 200%.

DoT.text:
DoT

	

		

		
	

	

	
		
Type

	
	

Combat

Damage Over Time
 (
DoT
) is a type of 
damage
 dealt through certain 
debuffs
 at the beginning of a target's turn. Unlike regular damage, DoT cannot score CRIT hits.

There are four basic types of DoT: 

 
Bleed
, 

 
Burn
, 

 
Shock
, and 

 
Wind Shear
, corresponding to 
Physical
, 
Fire
, 
Lightning
 and 
Wind
 respectively. Note that the 
Additional DMG
 dealt by 
Ice
's 

 Frozen and 
Quantum
's 

 Entanglement are 
not
 considered DoTs, despite being dealt at the beginning of the target's turn.

There are unique types of DoT exclusive to characters:

Black Swan
 is able to apply a unique DoT debuff known as 

 
Arcana
, which is regarded as Wind Shears, Bleed, Burn, and Shock effects at the same time.

Jiaoqiu
 is able to apply a unique debuff known as 

 
Ashen Roast
, which is regarded as a Burn effect.

There are two main sources of DoT: Character abilities and 
Weakness Break
. Depending on the source, DoT damage is calculated differently.

DoTs are dealt in chronological order based on when they are inflicted, with DoTs inflicted earlier dealt first; Arcana is the exception as it is always dealt at the end of the queue. When an enemy is defeated, the rest DoTs inflicted on them will not be dealt. 
Hysilens
's 
Zone
 allows her to directly deal 

 

Physical

 DoT after all other DoTs on the target have been dealt during DMG calculation.

Game Systems

Eidolons
 are successive upgrades to 
Characters
, which increase the effectiveness of the character or add new capabilities to existing abilities. 

Contents

1
 
Overview

2
 
How to Unlock

3
 
Other Languages

4
 
Navigation

Overview

[

]

Each character has a total of six Eidolon Resonance levels, with the third and fifth Eidolons always being a two-level increase to their 
Skill
, 
Ultimate
, 
Talent
 or a one-level increase to their 
Basic ATK
, 
Memosprite Skill
 or 
Memosprite Talent
. The first, second, fourth and sixth Eidolons can vary from pure stat increases, or the addition of new mechanics into a characters kit.

While within 
Currency Wars
, unlocked Eidolon levels will provide Off-Field characters with a different set of upgrades.

How to Unlock

[

]

See also: 
Eidolon (Item)
and
Shadow

To permanently unlock each Eidolon Resonance level of a character, the player must use the character's respective Eidolon item. Players may obtain a character's Eidolon upon obtaining a duplicate of the character, either through pulling from 
Warps
, purchasing from 
Starlight Exchange
, purchasing from 
Stellar Convergence
, or obtaining through completing 
Events
. 

The 
Trailblazer
's various Eidolon items, known as 
Shadows
, are uniquely obtained through completing 
Trailblaze Missions
, purchasing from 
World Shops
, 
Trailblaze Level
 rewards, levelling up the 
Tidal Bounty
, and 
As I've Written
.

Eidolon Resonance levels can also be temporarily obtained through event and gamemode mechanics, such as the Curio 
Space-Time Prism
, which gives all characters in the team one Eidolon level.

While the wearer is on the field, for every Elation character on the team, increases the Skill Point upper limit by 1, up to a max increase of 3. For every 1 Skill Point the wearer consumes, ignores 5~9% of enemy targets' DEF when this unit deals Elation DMG, stacking up to 4 times. If 4 or more Skill Points are consumed in the same turn, the wearer gains "Stream Promo," which increases all allies' Elation by 20~36%. Light Cone effects of the same type cannot stack.
OpeningIncreases the wearer's ATK by 20~40%. After the wearer uses their Skill or Ultimate on one ally character, increases the target's Elation stat by 12~24% for 2 turn(s).
RumbleIncreases the wearer's Elation by 12~20%. When the wearer uses an Elation Skill, increases Elation DMG taken by all enemies by 6~10% for 2 turn(s).

DecisionIncreases the wearer's CRIT Rate by 12~20%. When the wearer uses an Elation Skill, increases Elation by 12~20%, stacking up to 2 times.
CompanionIncreases the wearer's CRIT DMG by 12~24%. After the wearer uses their Ultimate, increases the Elation of all allies by 8~12%, lasting for 1 turn(s).

 Extra Turn

	

		

		
	

	

	
		
Type

	
	

Combat

Gain 1 extra turn that won't expend your remaining turns when taking action. During this extra turn, no Ultimate can be used.

Extra Turns
, indicated on the action bar by a star icon, are turns taken outside of a unit's normal turn order. When taking an Extra Turn, 
status effects
 will not tick down, and the unit's position on the action bar will not be affected. While using 
Ultimates
 is the most common way to obtain Extra Turns, certain other abilities may also grant Extra Turns which allow the usage of 
Basic ATKs
 or 
Skills
.

In general, Extra Turns have a higher priority than regular turns, but lower than 
Follow-Up Actions
. If multiple Extra Turns (including Ultimates) are performed, they are queued and performed in the order that they are triggered. Extra Turns from Skills that state "does not end the current turn" instead of "user gains an Extra Turn" are an exception to these, being pushed to behind the Extra Turn/Ultimate queue as if they were regular turns.

Overview

[

]

Memosprites are treated as individual units from the Memomaster. Unless otherwise specified, Memosprites share the same stats as their Memomaster. As an entity, they also have their place on the Action Order with a fixed 
Speed
 stat. 
Hyacine
's 
Little Ica
 and 
Cyrene
's 
Demiurge
 are exceptions to this, as they have 0 SPD, will not appear in the Action Order, and can only act if given an 
Extra Turn
. If specified in 
Memosprite Talent
, Memosprites can automatically use their Memosprite Skill when taking actions.

Unlike conventional summons, Memosprites are actual entities, meaning that they can be targeted for buffs/healing by allied characters. They also have an 
aggro
 value which allows enemies to target them. The only exception to this is 
Pollux
 due to it being a 
backup
 unit, which makes it unable to be targeted by enemy abilities. Memosprites are usually summoned through using the Memomaster's 
Skill
, but they can also be summoned by 
Ultimates
 or 
Techniques
. The Memosprite will persist on the field until their health fully depletes or until another specified condition is met, such as a countdown (Garmentmaker) or turn limit (Pollux), after which the Memomaster has to summon them again.

Memosprite Skill and Memosprite Talent are abilities unique to Memosprites that must be upgraded separately from the Memomaster's 
Traces
.

Unless otherwise specified, Memosprites inherit the base stats of their Memomasters in combat. However, Memosprites receive 
Status Effects
 separately from their Memomasters. Unless otherwise specified, Memosprites will also not receive most conditional stat bonuses found on the set effects of certain 
Relics
. Unless otherwise specified, abilities that affect the Memomaster do not affect the Memosprite, and vice versa. However, abilities that target all allies will affect both of them.

Since Memosprites are always summoned on the right side of their Memomaster, it is impossible for a Memosprite to be the first ally target in the team lineup.

Lore

The birth of an Aeon gives rise to a Path. The nature of the Paths remains a mystery, leaving us to draw an analogy in a way that mortals can understand: It's a philosophical concept of sorts.

 
Himeko

Paths
 are congregations of 
imaginary
 energy, born as manifestations of universal philosophical concepts. Upon ascension, an 
Aeon
 gains power over a specific Path, free to choose the allocation of imaginary energy towards that path however THEY wish.

1

A person is considered to be on a Path when their will overlaps with that Path. If the person has a strong enough will, they can draw power from it, becoming a 
Pathstrider
.

1

 The Path that they happen to follow will change in accordance with their own philosophies and opinions.

In gameplay, Paths have two classifications:

Paths associated with playable 
characters
 and 
Light Cones
 that generally describe their playstyle

Paths associated with 
Blessings
 in the 
Simulated
 and 
Divergent Universe
 game modes

Pathstriders

[

]

Main article: 
Pathstrider

A person is considered to be on a Path when their will overlaps with that Path. If the person has a strong enough will, they can draw power from that Path; those who can do so are called Pathstriders. Pathstriders possess extraordinary power, but are still insignificant when compared to the Aeons.

1

Emanators

[

]

Main article: 
Emanator

Emanators are individuals who have attained the permission of an Aeon to draw power from THEIR chosen Path. While not subservient to the Aeons, Emanators are as good as emissaries of the Aeons' wills in everyone else's eyes.

2

 Emanators have been stated and shown to be more powerful than regular Pathstriders, but their strength varies.

Different Aeons have different attitudes towards their Emanators; for instance, some Aeons regard Emanators as extensions of THEMSELVES and grant them much power, while other Aeons have no interest in creating Emanators. The Aeon 
Aha
 is said to grant mortals the power of THEIR Path at random in order to toy with them,

2

 while 
IX
 does not deliberately create Emanators, although Emanators of 
Nihility
 do exist due to Nihility enveloping everyone equally.

3

]

Description

[

]

Punchline is shared by the whole team. When dealing Elation DMG, the more Punchline taken into account, the higher the Elation DMG.

Punchline is typically generated by the abilities of 
Elation
 characters and certain enemies such as the 

 
Aggressive Reading Material

, though certain other battle effects may also contribute to the total. The team's tally is indicated by a graphic just above their 
Skill Points
.

If the team possesses Punchline, 
Aha
 will appear in the 
Action Bar
, and THEIR turn will trigger an Aha Instant which uses the team's Punchline tally to calculate the Elation DMG dealt. (The tally can increase during the Instant)

The Punchline multiplier for Elation DMG is as follows:

{\displaystyle {\text{Punchline Multiplier}}=1+{\frac {{\text{Punchline}}\times 5}{{\text{Punchline}}+240}}}

  

After the Aha Instant ends, the team's Punchlines are reset to 0, and participating characters gain an amount of 
Certified Banger
 equal to the amount of Punchline lost this way.

Aha Instants triggered by Aha's 
Extra Turns
 or alternate uses of 
Elation Skills
 are typically considered as using a fixed amount of Punchline for Elation DMG and Certified Banger conversion, and will 
not
 reset the team's count afterward.

When the battle starts or when Aha Instants end (following the conversion to Certified Banger if applicable), the team gains 1 Punchline for every 
Elation

Shield Stacking

[

]

If multiple shields are applied to the same character, they 
will not stack
, and the effective shield value of the character is equal to that of the shield with the highest value. When taking DMG, all applied shields will absorb the full amount of DMG simultaneously. A lower-value shield can break in the background while a higher-value shield remains.

If a background shield breaks, its corresponding shield status will disappear, alongside any additional effects that the status may have provided, such as the 
aggro
 increase from 
March 7th's shield
.

Skill Point.text:
Skill Point

	

		

		
	

	

	
		
Type

	
	

Combat

Skill Points
 are a type of resource shared by the player's team to perform Skills, represented by array(s) of four-point star icons. They are shared by the player's team.

The default number of Max Skill Points is 5, and the team starts with 3 Skill Points upon entering battle. If the maximum Skill Point is increased, the HUD will add empty stars, up to 10 stars, and if the current amount of Skill Points is more than 10, the 10th Skill Point star icon will be shown with another star behind it.

Most 
Skills
 consume a Skill Point to use, and most 
Basic Attacks
 generate a Skill Point. However, there are exceptions to the rule, such as enhanced Basic Attacks that do not generate and/or consume any Skill Points, and Skills that consume an alternative resource instead of Skill Points.

Certain characters, such as 
Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae
 and 
Sparxie
, have a personal resource named 
Squama Sacrosancta
 and 
Thrill
, respectively, which are shown on their character HUD, prioritized for consumption over standard Skill Points, and whose consumption is considered consuming an equal amount of Skill Points (for effects such as 
Yao Guang
's 
Talent
 and 
Propagation Blessings
).

Base Action Value is the time between turns for each unit and is calculated based on their SPD:

Turn order is determined as follows:

At the beginning of the battle, each unit's Action Value, representing the amount of time until that unit's next turn, is set to their Base Action Value.

At the beginning of the battle, effects that take effect upon entering battle, including SPD/AV modifying effects, are triggered on characters from left to right.

The unit with the lowest Action Value, i.e. shortest time until their next turn, is selected to be the next active unit.

All units subtract that lowest Action Value from their current Action Value, representing the progress of time until the next active unit's turn.

The active unit starts their turn. All 
DoTs
 on the active unit deal damage.

If the active unit is player-controlled and Auto mode is not enabled, the player has the opportunity to cast any pre-action Ultimate(s). Pre-action Ultimates 
cannot
 advance the action of the active unit (e.g. by the set effect of 
Eagle of Twilight Line
), since at this point the active unit's Action Value is already zero.

The active unit acts, resetting their Action Value to their Base Action Value. The player can queue any post-action Ultimates during the action animation.

Any post-action Ultimates queued during the action animation execute. Post-action Ultimates 
can
 advance the next action of the active unit, since at this point its Action Value has been reset.

The active unit's turn ends, ticking down any 
Status Effects
 on the active unit. Some Status Effects only tick down if they were present at the beginning of the active unit's turn.

Repeat from #3.

Over a long time, the number of turns a unit takes is proportional to their Speed.

full

Immediately Take Action

[

]

Effects described to make a target "immediately take action" are different from those that "forward action by 100%." Such effects forcibly set the current Action Value of the target to 0, regardless of their Action Value prior to that. Therefore, "immediately take action" effects will still fully advance the target even if their Action Value is greater than their Base Action Value due to action delay effects, while "forward action by 100%" effects do not.

However, if an "immediately take action" is applied during another character's turn, the current character will still need to finish their turn first before the target who had their action advanced can take action.

When a 
Boss Enemy
 or 
Echo of War Enemy
 with multiple phases enters a new phase, they will immediately take action.

Status Effect Duration

[

]

Some status effects unconditionally tick down at the end of the character's turn, while others only tick down if they were present at the start of that turn. All SPD modifying statuses fall into the latter category. For example, if 

 

Asta

 
Asta

 uses her Ultimate 

Astral Blessing

 
Astral Blessing

 in the middle of an ally's turn (including herself), the duration of Astral Blessing's SPD Boost will not decrease at the end of that ally's turn. The upshot is that using a SPD boost during the target character's turn gets the most out of its effect, whereas using it just before the target character's turn is the most wasteful.

]

Certain debuffs may fall under the following groups:

Crowd Control
: Debuffs that prevent a victim from taking extra actions and disable the victim's 
Ultimate
.

This includes Frozen, Entanglement, Imprisonment, Dominated, Outrage, and Strong Reverberation.

DoT
: Debuffs that cause a victim to take 
DoT
 (Damage Over Time) at the start of their turns.

This includes Bleed, Burn, Shock, and Wind Shear.

Note that Frozen and Entanglement are 
not

not
 considered DoT.

Slow
: Debuffs that decrease a victim's 
Speed
.

Weaken
: Debuffs that increase a victim's 
Weaken
, decreasing their 
DMG
 dealt.

Toughness
 is an enemy-only stat in 

Honkai: Star Rail

.

In combat, the Toughness gauge is displayed above the HP gauge of enemies. It can be reduced by attacks of a 
Type
 that the enemy is weak to. Once fully depleted, the enemy will suffer a 
Weakness Break
 which has the following effects:

Deals an instance of 
Break DMG

Delays the enemy's 
action
 by 25%

Has a 150% base chance to apply a 
debuff
 corresponding to the Type used to inflict Weakness Break

Enters the Weakness Broken state

In the enemy's next turn, they will recover from the Weakness Broken state and fully restores their Toughness gauge.

As long as the enemy is not Weakness Broken, all incoming DMG will be multiplied by 0.9, including the Break DMG from Toughness depletion.

Dealing Break DMG solely is 
not
 considered an attack.

Multi-Layered Toughness

[

]

Some enemies have multiple Toughness Bars. Fully depleting any Toughness Bar before the final one will only deal Break DMG without any other Weakness Break effects (action delay, Type-specific debuffs, entering the Weakness Broken state).

Exo-Toughness

[

]

 	

 	 	
 		 			

 		 		 		 			
A purple Exo-Toughness behind the initial Toughness.
 		 	
 

Exo-Toughness
 is an additional Toughness bar applied by certain effects, which is displayed behind the initial white Toughness. The initial Toughness needs to be depleted first (which triggers Weakness Break effects) before the Exo-Toughness can be reduced. Then, the Exo-Toughness can be reduced with any Type of attack regardless of Weaknesses, triggering Weakness Break again if depleted, which is equal to when depleting the original Toughness. Like the original Toughness, the Exo-Toughness can only be depleted once before recovering from Weakness Break. Effects that rely on Weakness Break such as 
Talents
, 
Bonus Abilities
 and 
Eidolons
 will also trigger when an Exo-Toughness bar is depleted.

When an enemy recovers from Weakness Break, Exo-Toughness will be fully restored, regardless of whether or not the Exo-Toughness bar was fully depleted.

Exo-Toughness was first introduced in 
Version 2.5
's 
Memory of Chaos
 iteration. In 
Version 2.7
, Exo-Toughness was made available for players as part of 
Fugue
's 
Talent
, 
Fortune Follows Where Virtue Spreads
.

Toughness Value and Reduction

[

]

Different enemies have varying amounts of Toughness. 
Normal
 enemies have the lowest Toughness, 
Elite
 enemies have much higher Toughness, and 
Boss
/
Echo of War
 enemies have the highest Toughness. The base Toughness value of most enemies is a multiple of 
10
, with the exception of some enemies with modified Toughness value in a certain phase. Sometimes, 10 
Toughness Reduction
 on display is also referred to as 1 Toughness Unit.

Different character skills will also deal varying amounts of Toughness Reduction. Currently, characters may deal 
1.666...
, 
2
,

,

,

,

 or 
40
 Toughness Reduction with their attacks. This does not account for skills and talents which can improve Weakness Break efficiency. 

Attacking an enemy in the overworld will deal 
10
 Toughness Reduction to all enemies weak to that attack's type upon entering battle. Certain 
Techniques
 can attack the enemy in the overworld and deal 
20
 Toughness Reduction to all enemies weak to that attack's type upon entering battle.

Some enemies are capable of locking their Toughness, though most of these are generally temporary until the according mechanic is lifted/removed.

Game Systems

Traces
 are skill trees that 
characters
 possess. Within the Traces menu, players can level up 
abilities
, unlock 
Bonus Abilities
, and increase stats.

The layout of Traces is determined by a character's 
Path
, with 
Remembrance
 and 
Elation
 featuring completely unique stat distributions. These skill trees allow players to upgrade 
Basic ATK
, 
Skill
, 
Ultimate
, and 
Talent
, unlock three 
Bonus Abilities
 at Character Ascension 2, 4, and 6, as well as a total of 10 stat boosts distributed across three character-specific stats. In addition, the skill trees also include an already unlocked 
Technique
. For 
Remembrance
, these upgrades are further divided into 
Memosprite Skill
 and 
Memosprite Talent
. For 
Elation
, an additional upgrade, the 
Elation Skill
, becomes available.

Currently, only three characters diverge from the standard Trace formula:

Castorice
's and 
Silver Wolf LV.999
's Talents also include their 
Exclusive Effects
, and their Trace tables feature unique artwork to reflect this.

Cyrene
's Memosprite Skill, 
This Ode, to All Lives
, features special artwork, and her Trace menu includes a dedicated interface that displays the full effects of the ability.

Trailblazer
's 
Remembrance
 Path is the only case of a character having a fourth 
Bonus Ability
, 
Unfinished Epilogue
, which is unlocked by completing 
Trailblaze Mission
 chapter 

As Tomorrow Became Yesterday

.

There are seven

 in

: 

Physical

, 

Fire

,

,

, 

Wind

, 

Quantum

, and 

Imaginary

. Each playable ally is assigned a single Type and their attacks deal matching DMG.

Enemies typically have 2 to 4 weaknesses to Types. Attacks of a Type they are weak to will reduce their 
Toughness
. When the enemy's Toughness is fully depleted, they will suffer a Weakness Break, taking an instance of Break DMG, likely receiving a debuff corresponding to the Type that caused the Weakness Break, and delaying their action. Such an enemy will stay in the Weakness Broken state until the start of their next turn, during which they will take 
11.111...%
 more DMG.

Allies do not have Toughness, and are unable to be inflicted with Weakness Break. However, Type-related debuffs can still be applied to allies by certain enemy attacks.

Vulnerability
, also known as 
DMG Taken
, is a hidden stat in 

Honkai: Star Rail

 that multiplicatively increases 
DMG
 taken by a target.

Vulnerability may apply to all DMG, a specific element, or DoTs. Different sources of Vulnerability stack additively.

Vulnerability can be modified by certain character abilities as well as special buffs such as those in the 
Simulated Universe
. Although the in-game wording for related effects is inconsistent, effects described to "increase DMG taken/received" generally modify the Vulnerability stat.
